# Weather, QBs, injuries, Kalshi {#sec-rounds45} @sec-improvements ended with a diagnosis: the gap to the market is **information, not modeling**. This chapter adds the information we could get for free and tests each piece with the same pre-registered rule. Every candidate was written down and committed before it was run (`docs/experiments/2026-09-24_*`). ## Does the market agree with us? Closing-line value Before adding anything, a measurement. Closing-line value (CLV) is how far the line moves toward a bet between the open (where we'd bet) and kickoff. A bettor whose lines keep moving their way has information the market later adopts, even in weeks when results go against them. ::: {#tbl-clv .cell tbl-cap='Closing-line value of the practice rules, out of sample 2021–2025 (points of line movement toward the bet).' execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
Bets Avg CLV Won vs open (%) Seasons with CLV > 0
Rule
Model 4+ points off the total 1064 0.45 54.2 5
Under in shootouts 514 -0.08 56.6 3
Every game, model's side 3941 0.19 51.0 4
``` ::: ::: The model's big disagreements with the opening total carry real information: the line moves toward them in every season. The shootout under is a different animal: it wins, but the line doesn't move toward it, a bias the market leaves in place all week. ## Round 4: weather and quarterbacks Weather: wind, rain and temperature over the 3.5 hours from kickoff, from the nearest weather station for past games (Meteostat) and the forecast for upcoming ones (Open-Meteo). Quarterbacks: the team's most recent starter, his experience and passing efficiency, and whether the starter just changed, from the passing box score. ::: {#tbl-round4 .cell tbl-cap='Round 4 candidates. Decision seasons 2021–2023, check seasons 2024–2025.' execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
Total 21–23 Margin 21–23 O/U 21–23 Total 24–25 O/U 24–25
A current 13.03 12.82 50.93 12.82 50.28
Q1 quarterbacks 13.00 12.84 50.45 12.81 51.16
W1 weather (raw) 12.99 12.83 50.11 12.80 52.29
W2 weather (thresholds) 13.00 12.83 50.80 12.84 51.60
``` ::: ::: ::: {#tbl-round4-verdict .cell tbl-cap='Round 4 verdicts (primary metric: total MAE for weather, margin MAE for quarterbacks).' execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
Metric Seasons better Gain, 95% interval Adopted
W1 weather (raw) total MAE 3 [+0.008, +0.064] True
W2 weather (thresholds) total MAE 3 [+0.000, +0.054] True
Q1 quarterbacks margin MAE 0 [-0.052, +0.009] False
``` ::: ::: Weather improves total-points error in all three decision seasons and was **adopted**. W2 (the same idea as thresholds) also passed, with a weaker interval; only the stronger version, W1, went into the model. The gain is small, and it lowers the error more than it moves the O/U record, which goes down in 2021–23 and up in 2024–25. Quarterback features add nothing the team ratings don't already carry. ## Round 5: an injury proxy No free source publishes college football injury reports as data. The closest thing is the box score: a key player (the QB, top two rushers, top three receivers, top three tacklers) who had stats earlier in the season but **none in his team's previous game**. ::: {#tbl-round5 .cell tbl-cap='Round 5: key-player availability (primary metric: margin MAE).' execution_count=5} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
Metric Seasons better Gain, 95% interval Adopted
I1 availability margin MAE 1 [-0.021, +0.031] False
I1 (total, info only) total MAE 2 [-0.020, +0.030] False
``` ::: ::: Not adopted. Many of those players return the next week, and when they don't, the news reaches the line before kickoff. The flag stays on the website as information. ## Kalshi: halves, quarters and team totals Kalshi lists what our sportsbook data doesn't. Two findings came before any bet: 1. **Split the market, don't replace it.** Each team's points implied by the sportsbook line, split across halves and quarters by the model's shares, beat the period models in every period. The period models alone predicted medians, so their quarters summed to about 47 points against about 53 for the full game. 2. **Honest ladders.** The chance a period lands over any line comes from the model's out-of-sample errors; on 2024–2025 lines the calibration error is under 3.5 points. Then the test that matters: real Kalshi prices from 2026 weeks 1–3, four hours before kickoff, with the pre-registered rules. ::: {#tbl-kalshi .cell tbl-cap='Kalshi backtest, 2026 weeks 1–3 (profit after fees).' execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
Bets Win % ROI %
Tier
Best 127 52.8 4.3
Lean 173 49.7 -6.9
Everything else 1470 53.1 -3.9
Best + Lean 300 51.0 -2.3
``` ::: ::: On all 1836 main lines, Kalshi's own prices predicted outcomes slightly better than the model (Brier 0.224 vs 0.2256). Not adopted for picks: the site shows Kalshi prices next to the model's chance as information, and the would-be picks are logged on paper so the 2026 season can settle it. ## Where that leaves us The information that would close the gap (who is actually playing this week) isn't available for free. What was available (weather) went in, and what didn't help was documented and left out. The recommendations stay where the evidence is: totals, and only when the win chance clears 54%.
